V8 Anatomy

A front-view guide to the major V8 assemblies, from covers and heads to pistons, rods, crank, and block.

Explore the V8 Engine

Valve covers

Valve covers seal the upper valvetrain area and help keep the cylinder head assembly contained.

Cylinder heads

Cylinder heads guide the combustion process and contain the intake and exhaust passages of each bank.

Pistons + connecting rods

The pistons and rods turn the combustion force into crankshaft rotation and are arranged in the two V-bank rows.

Crankshaft

The crankshaft converts the pistons' reciprocating motion into rotating output at the engine's center.

Engine block

The block is the structural base of the engine and positions the cylinders, crankshaft, and head assemblies.
